Our findings emphasize the need to construct confidence intervals for a specified estimand and performance measure.

nominations.title: A Consistent Bayesian Adaptive Quotient Graph Framework for Graph-Informed Random Partition Models
nominations.authors: Kun Huang, Xiyu Peng, Huiyan Sang
nominations.abstract: Bayesian graph-informed random partition models are widely used to model heterogeneity in structured data. A prominent approach assigns a prior directly on the space of contiguous partitions of a pre-determined graph G; however, such models are not data-adaptive and can be computationally infeasible for large graphs. To address these limitations, we propose a Bayesian adaptive quotient graph framework that induces partitions through a two-level hierarchical prior: a prior is first imposed on quotient graphs of G, followed by a conditional prior on a reduced contiguous partition space induced by each quotient graph. We develop high-level assumptions that guide the construction of the two-level prior such that the reduced space retains desirable partitions. We further establish high-level assumptions for posterior concentration on desirable quotient graphs and partitions. The framework can be readily embedded into many existing Bayesian hierarchical models with latent cluster structures as a contiguous random partition prior. As a specific example, we apply the proposed framework to the spatial random partition model proposed in Huang and Sang (2026). The resulting model adapts to the unknown number of clusters, achieves a faster clustering-consistency contraction rate, and yields substantially lower partition error and computation time in simulations. Finally, we apply the resulting model to a large spatial transcriptomics dataset to demonstrate its practical utility.

nominations.title: Stratified Randomization Incorporating Historical Control Data
nominations.authors: Masatoshi Shoji, Isao Yokota, Carolin Herrmann
nominations.abstract: Randomized controlled trials are often infeasible in rare diseases because of limited sample size, high costs, or lengthy durations. Hybrid control designs address this by combining a concurrent control arm with historical data. However, existing methods such as propensity score matching (PSM) borrow historical data only at the analysis stage, which limits power gains when covariate distributions differ between historical and concurrent data. We propose a stratified block randomization method for hybrid control trials. Within each stratum, more concurrent subjects are allocated to the treatment arm than to the concurrent control arm, and the difference is filled with historical controls so that the treatment and hybrid control arms are balanced 1:1; once the available historical controls in the stratum are used or a pre-specified overall cap is reached, allocation returns to 1:1. Historical controls are incorporated either by sampling or by weighting. We compared both methods with PSM in terms of type I error rate, power, and sample size via Monte Carlo simulations. The sampling method maintained the type I error rates when there was neither heterogeneity in the outcome model nor unmeasured covariates. It also had power comparable to or greater than that of PSM, particularly when historical controls were unevenly distributed across strata. The power of the weighting method increased with the pooled historical sample size, but its type I error rate was inflated when covariates beyond the stratification factors were present or when stratification factors were dichotomized from continuous covariates. The proposed method incorporates historical data at the allocation stage rather than only at the analysis stage, enabling more efficient use of historical data.

nominations.title: evgmrf: An R Package For Gaussian Markov Random Field Extreme Value Models
nominations.authors: Benjamin D. Youngman, Ayu Shabrina
nominations.abstract: We introduce \textsf{evgmrf}, an \textsf{R} package for fitting spatially varying extreme value models using Gaussian Markov random fields (GMRFs). The package supports the generalized extreme value distribution for block maxima, the generalized Pareto distribution for threshold exceedances, the Poisson--GPD point-process model, and the $r$-largest order-statistics model. Distributional parameters may vary over regular spatial grids or arbitrary regions that can be represented by a valid adjacency matrix, with optional fixed effects and covariate dependence. Spatial structure is represented through intrinsic conditional autoregressive, proper conditional autoregressive, and Besag--York--Molli\'{e} 2 models, which are extended with non-Gaussian random-effect distributions. Estimation uses penalized likelihood with smoothing or dependence hyper-parameters estimated using a Laplace approximation, exploiting sparse precision matrices for computational efficiency. The package provides methods for model summaries, spatial visualization, prediction on link and response scales, estimation of extreme quantiles, and uncertainty quantification in the form of approximate standard error estimates, or via simulations from parameter sampling distributions. Examples based on gridded and county-level precipitation data illustrate the use of the package for spatial modelling of environmental extremes. \textsf{evgmrf} provides a unified, accessible framework for extreme value analyses in which distributional parameters exhibit structured spatial variation.

nominations.title: Cross-Fitted Doubly Robust Estimation with Student-t Outcome Engines: ECM Algorithms, Monte Carlo Evidence and Schistosomiasis Programme Data from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
nominations.authors: Cosmas Kambale Musambi, Ernest Fokou\'e
nominations.abstract: Routine data on preventive chemotherapy for schistosomiasis are confounded, clustered, heavy-tailed and heaped. We study how cross-fitted augmented inverse probability weighted (AIPW) estimators behave, and how they should be computed, when least squares is replaced by Student-t outcome engines: Huber and t iteratively reweighted least squares, and a two-component t scale-mixture regression fitted by an ECM algorithm, alongside a residual-clipped augmentation. We give four short propositions (exact AIPW bias, the efficiency bound, the estimand of clipping, monotone ascent of a scale-constrained ECM), a single-file Python implementation with cluster-level cross-fitting, cluster-robust standard errors and a cluster bootstrap, and a Monte Carlo study with up to 1000 replications per cell. Robust outcome engines leave AIPW unchanged (RMSE differences at most 0.002), whereas clipping cuts RMSE by 26-45% under symmetric contamination, under-covers, and, as a plasmode experiment built on real covariates and residuals shows, shifts the estimand when residual laws differ between arms. One-sided artefacts that differ between arms bias every estimator. Heaped data also break naive code: the MAD scale collapses and the mixture likelihood is unbounded, and we give simple guards. Applied to 1485 rounds in 362 health zones of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (ESPEN, 2014-2025), integrated delivery appears to raise programme coverage by 17.4 percentage points, yet epidemiological coverage differs by only 0.9: the gap comes from targeting denominators, a real differential artefact that no outcome engine can remove.

nominations.title: Identification and Inference of Bi-directional Causal Effects in Mendelian Randomization without Instrument Selection
nominations.authors: Liyuan Mo, Qingyuan Zhao
nominations.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instruments to estimate causal effects. Bidirectional MR usually uses two reversed unidirectional analyses, but feedback can invalidate instruments in at least one direction and induce correlated pleiotropy. We model both traits as a stable cyclic system and estimate both directional effects from GWAS summary data without instrument selection or a prespecified valid-instrument subset. After LD score normalisation, marginal associations form a heteroscedastic noisy independent component analysis model, assuming the variants' direct effects on the two traits are independent. If those effects are non-Gaussian, this identifies the total-effect matrix up to scaling and permutation; no-self-feedback and stability of the system further resolve these ambiguities. We develop an estimator based on noise-adjusted second- and fourth-order moments, avoiding inversion of the high-dimensional linkage disequilibrium matrix and having computational cost linear in the number of variants. Under weak local dependence, we establish consistency, asymptotic normality, and validity of a chromosome-respecting moving block bootstrap. Simulations show negligible bias, generally reliable interval coverage, and higher rejection rates for nonzero directional effects than focusing-based tests. Three real-data applications illustrate how joint analysis of feedback systems can yield causal decompositions differing from two separate unidirectional analyses.

nominations.title: Comments on: `CliPS: How to identify cluster distributions in Bayesian mixture models'
nominations.authors: Sara Wade
nominations.abstract: I congratulate the authors on their contribution, which addresses important challenges in understanding posterior distributions in Bayesian mixture models. As underlined by the authors, the Bayesian framework has several advantages, yet label-switching, identifiability issues, and the trans-dimensional nature of parameter spaces make exploiting the Bayesian approach and understanding the resulting posterior difficult in practice. The paper offers clear explanations and a simple, intuitive procedure to address this by clustering the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) draws of component-specific parameters. It is clearly illustrated on several examples.

nominations.title: A fast and sound algorithm to simplify summations in interventional queries expressions
nominations.authors: Ivano Lodato, Simran Hiranandani, Aditya Varna Iyer
nominations.abstract: Identification formulas returned by the ID algorithm often contain summations that can be removed. The procedure proposed in arxiv:1806.07082 (TK) removes them by combining factors of the formula into joint distributions, through the chain rule and through the insertion of factors for missing variables. We make two changes to this procedure: only the factors that involve the summed variable are combined, and every factor is written with a minimal conditioning set. These two changes determine the rest of the procedure, in which each search over a power set is replaced by a single test and the variables to insert are fixed in advance, and they remove summations that the TK procedure leaves in place. The resulting procedure is sound and, for minimal input terms, complete for each individual elimination with respect to joins and insertions.

nominations.title: Constrained Stochastic Policy Targeting under Heterogeneous Partial Interference
nominations.authors: Elena Dal Torrione, Chan Park, Laura Forastiere
nominations.abstract: Under heterogeneous interference, treating individuals with particular characteristics affects the population average outcome through their heterogeneous direct response to treatment and indirect effect on others, creating opportunities for efficient policy design. For instance, policymakers may minimize resource use by vaccinating individuals identified as superspreaders to achieve a target reduction in disease incidence. In such setting, we first study the problem of learning individualized stochastic treatment policies that minimize population average treatment probability subject to a prespecified outcome target. We propose an estimation approach based on a smooth surrogate for constraint violations and interference-aware inverse-probability-weighting or self-normalized estimators of the population average outcome, and establish finite-sample regret guarantees for both estimators. We also consider the complementary problem of maximizing the population average outcome subject to a constraint on average treatment probability. We apply the proposed methodology to a Colombian conditional cash transfer program aimed at improving school attendance. The application demonstrates that accounting for interference and individualizing treatment probabilities can reduce resource use relative to policies that ignore interference or impose homogeneous treatment probabilities.

nominations.title: Hidden Markov Models for Dynamic Co-Clustering
nominations.authors: Shuchismita Sarkar, Jing Li, Michael P. B. Gallaugher, Xuwen Zhu
nominations.abstract: To jointly identify temporal regimes and row-column structure in matrix-valued time series, we propose a hidden Markov model (HMM) with Gaussian co-clustering distributions. A single latent regime governs each matrix. Conditional on the regime, row and column memberships define Gaussian blocks, each with its own mean and variance. Membership probabilities and block parameters are shared across occurrences of a regime, while individual memberships may vary between time points.

nominations.title: Dynamic bigraphical Mat\'ern--Whittle processes: learning dependence graphs among spatial-temporal fields
nominations.authors: Alokesh Manna, Debangan Dey
nominations.abstract: Many studies record several variables at the same sites over a sequence of periods, such as pollutant concentrations at monitoring stations or case counts of infectious diseases by district. A central question concerns the dependence between the variables and its change over time. We develop dynamic bigraphical Mat\'ern--Whittle (DBMW) processes for such data. Each variable has a spatial field that evolves by autoregression. A graph over the variables couples the temporal innovations of the fields. Its links appear and vanish over time, and a link may change sign. A graph Laplacian on the sites gives the spatial structure, and a canonical exponential family links the fields to Gaussian, count or binomial responses. The joint distribution of the latent fields over all sites, variables and periods factorizes over the eigenmodes of the graph Laplacian, and its normalizing constant is free of the graph and of the dynamics. Given the fields, the posterior of the time-varying signed graph is therefore exact, by forward--backward recursions. The estimator has three steps: a fit without a graph, which also gives the switching rates with an interval, the exact graph posterior, and a joint refit. In simulations, DBMW recovers the graph with higher average precision than graphical lasso, time-varying graphical lasso and Poisson log-normal networks, and it predicts withheld data better than a standard spatio-temporal model that fits each variable separately, with a Mat\'ern field and autoregressive evolution, by integrated nested Laplace approximation. In weekly air-quality data from 288 U.S. sites, it recovers the seasonal change of sign between ozone and nitrogen dioxide. In German surveillance data on seven diseases, the district-level links stay positive and stable through the COVID-19 pandemic.

nominations.title: Minimaxity in Robust Nonparametric Regression: from Heavy-Tailed to Sub-Gaussian Assumptions
nominations.authors: Yikun Li, Matey Neykov
nominations.abstract: We study nonparametric regression over star-shaped function classes under strong adversarial contamination. The clean (original) observations $(\tilde{X} _{i},\tilde{Y} _{i})_{i=1} ^{n}$ are i.i.d. and satisfy $\tilde{Y} _{i}=f ^{*}(\tilde{X} _{i})+\xi _{i}$, where $f ^{*}\in \mathcal{F}$, $\tilde{X}$ is distributed as $\mathbb{P} _{X}$, and the noise is conditionally centered. An adversary may inspect the clean sample and replace at most $\lfloor \epsilon n\rfloor$ observation pairs. We assume that $\mathcal{F}\subset L _{2}(\mathbb{P} _{X})$ is star-shaped with finite diameter $d$. Under a Bernstein-type moment condition on function increments and a bounded conditional second moment for the noise, we establish the matching lower and upper bounds of order $\left((\eta ^{*}) ^{2} \vee \epsilon \right)\wedge d ^{2}$, uniformly over admissible star-shaped function classes, therefore characterizing the minimax rate of estimation error, where \begin{equation*} \eta ^{*}:=\sup\left\{\eta >0: n\eta^2\leq\log \mathcal M _{\mathcal{F}}^{\text{loc}}(\eta,c)\right\}. \end{equation*} Here $\log \mathcal{M} _{\mathcal{F}} ^{\text{loc}}(\eta,c)$ denotes the local metric entropy of $\mathcal{F}$ in $L _2(\mathbb{P} _{X})$, and $c$ is a sufficiently large constant. Under a uniform relative sub-Gaussian condition on function increments and noise, the lower bound is adjusted to $\left((\eta ^{*})^{2}\vee \epsilon ^{2}\right)\wedge d ^{2}$ while the upper bound improves to $\left((\eta ^{*})^{2}\vee \epsilon ^{2}\log ^{2}\left(\frac{e}{\epsilon }\right)\right)\wedge d ^{2}$, yielding minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors.

nominations.title: High-Dimensional Gaussian and Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates with General Covariance
nominations.authors: Miles E. Lopes, Ricardo Masini
nominations.abstract: We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of $n$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order $1/\sqrt n$ are attainable up to factors of $\log(pn)$ when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.

nominations.title: Statistical guarantees for signature kernel ridge regression
nominations.authors: Christian Bayer, Jakob Kellermann
nominations.abstract: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.

nominations.title: Characterizing M-estimators using canonical divergences from information geometry
nominations.authors: Paul Navas
nominations.abstract: On Euclidean space, the losses that produce consistent M-estimators of a functional are its strictly consistent scoring functions (Dimitriadis, Fissler and Ziegel, 2024), and Osband's principle characterizes these through identification functions, which define method-of-moments estimators. We extend this characterization to the probability simplex. We define the residual, which on Euclidean space is a subtraction, as the inverse exponential map of an affine connection. It identifies the exponential barycenter of the connection: the arithmetic, normalized geometric and Fr\'echet means for the mixture, exponential and Levi-Civita connections. Its integral along geodesics is the canonical divergence of Ay and Amari (2015). A geometric form of Osband's principle decides which losses each connection admits. For the flat connections every strictly convex generator yields a consistent Bregman loss. For the curved $\alpha$-connections, half the squared Fisher-Rao distance is (up to scale) the only consistent loss for the Fr\'echet mean, and for $\alpha \notin \{-1, 0, 1\}$ no such loss exists and only the method of moments remains. The residual is integrable only at $\alpha = 0$, sharpening the integrability claim of Ay and Amari. The characterization yields the estimating equations of regression on the simplex and the calibration decomposition of compositional forecasts.

nominations.title: Causal and conditional tail coefficients: asymptotics, inference and graph recovery
nominations.authors: Axel B\"ucher, Mario Krali
nominations.abstract: The causal tail coefficient (CTC) measures the influence of an extreme value of one variable on another variable and has been proposed as a tool for causal discovery in heavy-tailed models. Despite its popularity, the asymptotic behavior of its empirical counterpart has not been well understood. We develop an asymptotic theory for the rank-based CTC estimator with an intermediate threshold under nonparametric conditions that are satisfied by all standard copula models. A key observation is that the CTC is determined by the mean of a conditional tail limit distribution, which clarifies its interpretation and determines the asymptotic variance of the estimator. We establish joint asymptotic normality for the entire CTC matrix and prove consistency of a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference. For heavy-tailed linear and recursive max-linear structural equation models, we show that the CTC equals one if and only if the first variable is an ancestor of the second, which leads to confidence graphs for the ancestral graph with asymptotic coverage guarantees. All results extend to general conditional tail coefficients, defined as further functionals of the conditional tail limit distribution. A simulation study and an application to dietary intake data illustrate the methods.

nominations.title: Quantifying Dependence Effects on $k$-out-of-$n$ Reliability Relative to the Independent Benchmark
nominations.authors: Nuria Torrado
nominations.abstract: Understanding how dependence among component lifetimes affects the reliability of redundant systems is a central problem in reliability engineering. In this paper, we develop a framework for quantifying the impact of multivariate dependence on $k$-out-of-$n$ system reliability relative to the independent benchmark. Using an orthogonal Legendre expansion of the copula density, we derive an exact decomposition that separates the dependence structure from the system architecture. This representation identifies how individual dependence contributions are transmitted to system reliability through explicit structural weights. An application to multivariate Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copulas demonstrates that higher-order dependence can produce distinct reliability effects even when all bivariate copulas remain unchanged. Our findings provide a systematic approach to quantifying and interpreting the effects of multivariate dependence on the reliability of redundant systems.

nominations.title: Orthogonal Scores and Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Possibly Misspecified GMM
nominations.authors: Byunghoon Kang
nominations.abstract: We develop Neyman orthogonal scores for GMM models that remain valid when the moment conditions may fail to hold. Existing score constructions typically require the moment conditions to hold exactly, which may fail in over-identified models, where the number of moment functions exceeds the number of parameters. We construct \emph{misspecification-robust} orthogonal score that has a closed form; it is the conventional orthogonal score plus adjustment terms, for the estimation of the Jacobian and of the weighting matrix, which are proportional to the population moment and vanish under correct specification. The moment functions may depend on nonparametric or machine learning first steps, and we show that double/debiased machine learning (DML) combined with the proposed scores and cross-fitting provides uniformly valid inference for a low-dimensional GMM estimand, while the conventional DML standard errors are inconsistent when the moment conditions fail. We illustrate the results in the partially linear instrumental variables (PLIV) model and in the local average treatment effects (LATE) model with multiple instruments.

nominations.title: Random Utility Models in the Consumption-Budget Setting: Vertex and Network-Flow Characterizations
nominations.authors: Haoge Chang, Kota Saito, Mingxi Zhu
nominations.abstract: This note supplements our paper \textit{Alternative Computational Formulations for Testing Discrete-Choice Random Utility Models: Half-Space and Network-Flow Formulations} and serves two purposes: 1. We clarify the conceptual distinctions between two classes of random utility models (RUM): those in the consumption-budget setting \citep{kitamura2019nonparametric} (hereafter KS) and those in the finite-alternative setting (e.g., Chapter~7 of \cite{chambers2016revealed}). In particular, we show (Theorem 1) that each rational type, as defined in KS, can be obtained as a coordinate projection of the deterministic choice vector induced by a strict preference ranking that satisfies what we call a patch-monotonicity condition. 2. We generalize the network-flow characterization for finite-alternative RUM in \cite{fiorini2004short} to the consumption-budget setting (Theorem 2). Specifically, we show that a vector of choice probabilities in the consumption-budget setting is rationalizable in the KS sense if and only if it is the image of a unit flow on a multi-arc powerset digraph under a fixed linear map. The key distinction is that our digraph allows multiple arcs between the same pair of nodes, whereas the digraph in Fiorini has at most one arc between any pair of nodes.

nominations.title: Positive Weights Do Not Certify TWFE Inference: A Design Diagnostic under Treatment-Effect Heterogeneity
nominations.authors: Stanis{\l}aw M. S. Halkiewicz
nominations.abstract: Conventional two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) inference need not be uniformly adequate even when all treatment weights are positive. Under a local treatment-effect drift, the statistic for the equally weighted treated-cell effect has worst-case mean shift $(c/q)\Gamma$, where $\Gamma=\sqrt{N_1}\|w-u\|_2$ is design-only and $q$ is the cluster-score noise scale. Projection matches the exposure to cohort, event-time, additive, and saturated group-time pilots; when residualized treatment is constant within treated group-time cells, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{gt}}=\Gamma$. A direct score estimator is feasible with fixed panel length as clusters grow. Because a debiased quadratic pilot is nonregular at zero, we use two regular one-sided procedures: a reverse-triangle multiplier lower bound to detect unsafe envelopes and covariance-aware noncentral-$\chi^2$ inversion to certify adequacy. At $5\%$ nominal size with a five-point tolerance, the shift threshold is $0.652$. In the Callaway--Sant'Anna minimum-wage panel, where every treated-cell weight is positive, the saturated $95\%$ lower shift bound is $0.793$, so conventional inference is not uniformly certified. A complementary Brazilian property-tax reanalysis with $2{,}840$ municipalities withholds certification in all four classes; its smallest lower bound is $1.040$. Under the maintained many-cluster approximation, castle-doctrine homicide passes for additive cohort-plus-event-time heterogeneity with a $95\%$ upper bound of $0.236$; its saturated covariance lacks one required rank. Divorce is inconclusive. These envelopes are not predictions of realized rejection. The diagnostic separates point correction, uniform exposure, and statistically warranted certification.

nominations.title: Broken Adaptive Ridge in High-Dimensional Vector Autoregressions
nominations.authors: Gianluca Cubadda, Luca Margaritella, Orest Prifti
nominations.abstract: We study regularized estimation in high-dimensional vector autoregressions under physical dependence and row-wise approximate sparsity using the Broken Adaptive Ridge (BAR) estimator. BAR is an iteratively reweighted Ridge procedure whose fixed-point first-order conditions imply a coordinatewise thresholding rule that produces exact zeros. We show that the BAR estimation error can be analyzed on the union of the population support above the BAR threshold and the support selected in the sample. The size of this union can be controlled at the rate implied by approximate sparsity, allowing us to establish the required restricted-curvature condition and derive L1, L2, and prediction error rates when the number of regressors grows polynomially with the sample size and may exceed it. Under exact sparsity, the resulting rates recover the familiar rates for sparse high-dimensional estimation. Monte Carlo experiments across a range of high-dimensional VAR designs show that BAR delivers strong estimation and forecasting performance, and retains a high share of relevant coefficients relative to Lasso, adaptive Lasso, and SCAD. An application to U.S. inflation forecasting using FRED-MD shows particularly strong performance at the one-month horizon.

nominations.title: Estimating a Rational Inattention Discrete Choice Model: A Semiparametric Approach
nominations.authors: Hanqi Wang
nominations.abstract: People's choices depend on both the payoffs of the available options and what they learn about those payoffs before deciding. This paper shows how choice data identify both unobserved payoff heterogeneity and the cost of information acquisition in a rational inattention discrete-choice model. I establish conditions for semiparametric point identification using exogenous payoff and information-cost shifters, without imposing parametric forms on the taste-shock distribution or on how the unit cost of information varies with observed characteristics. In the model with binary choice, I construct an unobserved choice threshold whose cumulative distribution function is the choice probability as a function of the payoff shifter. Moments of this threshold identify the payoff coefficients and the unit cost of information at each value of the information-cost shifter. A deconvolution argument then identifies the taste-shock distribution. I then extend identification to the model with multinomial choice. To estimate the model, I propose a sieve minimum-distance estimator based on observed market shares and establish its consistency. For inference, I construct confidence regions by test inversion because binding parameter constraints can make the estimator's limiting distribution nonnormal. In an application to Amazon Mechanical Turk, model counterfactuals show that lower unit costs of information raise the average task-taking probability and reduce wage elasticity.

nominations.title: AI and the Two Margins of Work: Why Job Losses Show Up Before Job Creation
nominations.authors: Mark Esposito, Liu Zhang
nominations.abstract: Technological change acts on labor demand at two margins: adjustment within established activities and the creation of additional activities, often by new firms. Payroll statistics record the first promptly and the second late. In the computing era, firms that entered in 1978 or later held 42 percent of payroll by 1998 and entering cohorts kept about 80 percent of their payroll after five years; in the industries most exposed to automation, incumbents contracted before entrants accumulated, a sequence that is precise early in the period and suggestive by its end. We develop a model in which one AI capability lowers the full cost of acceptable output in existing production and makes additional projects worth attempting, with founder effort separate from hired hours. If operating products re-scale instantly, automation displaces no aggregate hours; if they take time, hours fall first and recover as incumbents re-expand and new products arrive, with the long-run sign set by income effects. Establishment job flows through the first quarter of 2026 show no gradient on language-model exposure on either margin, which is what the model predicts under the observed adoption path and also what no effect on payroll would look like; studies with founding-task exposure find entry rising 10 to 20 percent. We propose a net reinstatement ratio and show that statistics which record new work late overstate displacement for years.

nominations.title: Menu Design Meets Market Design: Strategic Simplicity vs. Choice Complexity
nominations.authors: Gian Caspari, Paul Erg\"un Hild, Michael Hilweg-Waldeck, Manshu Khanna, Vincent Meisner
nominations.abstract: Strategic simplicity removes the incentive to misreport preferences, but it does not ensure that participants can identify what they prefer. We study this distinction in a laboratory experiment on serial dictatorships, where optimal play only requires choosing one's favorite bundle of real-effort tasks. Participants make fifteen incentivized choices among bundles that vary in how many tasks they combine. They choose either from a large menu or through a series of binary choices. Having made all choices, they unexpectedly reconsider each assignment against a previously rejected alternative. We find that roughly one in six choices is reversed and almost one in five involves an objectively dominated bundle. Simplifying the choice architecture does not help. Binary decomposition even raises reversal rates among low-ability participants and further inflates their confidence about their choices.

nominations.title: COPASI Skills: Agent Skills for COPASI analyses through Basico
nominations.authors: Frank T. Bergmann, Sven Sahle
nominations.abstract: Biochemical models represent biological systems as networks of reactions that describe the production, consumption, and transformation of molecular species over time. These models provide a quantitative framework for analyzing system dynamics and enable computational experiments that complement traditional wet-lab approaches, helping researchers gain mechanistic insight and make predictive assessments of biological behavior. COPASI is a widely used program for simulating and analyzing those models. These tasks are made availabe to Python through Basico. COPASI Skills is a set of instruction files that tell an assistant how to drive Basico for one analysis at a time. Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file. A short description at the top tells the assistant when the skill applies, and the rest of the file states which calls to make, which files to write, and which potential neighboring skill to choose additionally. A researcher can ask for example, in ordinary language, for a time course, a fit, or a published model. The assistant follows the matching skill and leaves tables or a report next to the model. The collection is released under a two-clause BSD license from [https://github.com/fbergmann/copasi-skills](https://github.com/fbergmann/copasi-skills).

nominations.title: Physical-Risk-Aware Decentralized Agents for Constrained Vehicle Communications
nominations.authors: Haoran Peng, William Weijia Zheng, Hang Liu, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang
nominations.abstract: Decentralized V2X resource control is challenging because each vehicle has only local observations, while reliability depends on network-wide interactions. We develop a physical-risk-aware spatio-temporal graph attention (PA-STGAT) framework for agentic V2X control. Each vehicle perceives its local interaction graph, retains short-term temporal context, and independently selects its PC5 resource and power. Network outcomes are used during centralized training to refine the shared policy. Transmitter-specific credits map reliability failures to individual vehicles. A dual-priced graph term further converts network violations into coordination signals for discrete resource selection, with higher priority on short time-to-collision links. Experiments show higher raw-policy reliability than the tested graph-based baselines. Under filtered execution, PA-STGAT meets the nominal empirical communication requirements across all five seeds, with tradeoffs among utility, delivery reliability, resource occupancy, and filter-induced repair. Compared with GNN+MATD3, it requires fewer resource repairs but achieves lower utility and mean delivery reliability. Mechanism ablations show that removing dual-priced graph coordination causes resource-selection collapse. Density and mobility tests characterize the operating limits of empirical constraint satisfaction.

nominations.title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
nominations.authors: Yunseob Tae, Jeongjae Lee, Songnam Hong
nominations.abstract: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

nominations.title: Brain-inspired Beam Selection for mmWave RIS Communication
nominations.authors: Aris Karampelas Timotijevic, Christos G. Tsinos, Alexandros-Apostolos A. Boulogeorgos, Theodoros A. Tsiftsis
nominations.abstract: Beam selection at large passive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) requires either full channel knowledge or beam training, both of which entail unwanted overhead. On the other hand, learned models that predict the optimal codeword from channels sampled at a few active elements avoid both, at the cost of energy-demanding multiply-and-accumulate operations. In this paper, we propose spiking neural network (SNN)-based beam selection for a semi-active RIS assisting a mmWave multiple-input single-output communication system. Direct and sigmoid rate coding are compared against a multi- layer perceptron (MLP) of identical architecture. Energy analysis further reveals that the input layer dominates SNN energy consumption.

nominations.title: Efficient Design of Flag Sequence Sets for Delay-Doppler Estimation via Riemannian Optimization
nominations.authors: Xuyang Zhao, Zeping Sui, Zilong Liu, Jiangtao Wang, Yongchao Wang
nominations.abstract: This letter investigates the design of a Flag sequence set with peak-curtain auto-ambiguity functions to enable low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Given the predefined Curtain sequences, the Flag sequence set design problem is formulated as the minimization of the weighted integrated masked sidelobe level. To solve this problem, we first reformulate it as an unconstrained optimization problem on the unimodular manifold. Then, a tailored unimodular manifold conjugate gradient (UM-CG) algorithm is developed. Compared with the existing define algorithm, the proposed UM-CG algorithm reduces computational and storage requirements. Moreover, the global convergence of the proposed UM-CG scheme is theoretically derived under mild conditions. Numerical results demonstrate the superior optimization performance of the proposed UM-CG algorithm and show that the designed Flag sequences exhibit nearly ideal peak-curtain properties.

nominations.title: Constant-Weight Sparse Vector Coded Augmented-AFDM
nominations.authors: Zhou Lu, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Lie-liang Yang
nominations.abstract: Sparse vector coding (SVC) and its variants convey information through sparse vectors (SVs), or sparse support patterns and detecting information by solving sparse recovery problems, making them attractive for short-packet ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC). However, as the required information rate increases, conventional SVC schemes or the enhanced SVC (ESVC) schemes require a rapidly growing number of SVs, resulting in significant increase of complexity and receiver processing latency. On the other hand, when communicating in doubly selective channels, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) suffers from the Doppler spread induced inter-carrier interference, while affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) experiences the same peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) problem as OFDM, although it allows diversity gain from channel's double selectivity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a constant-weight sparse vector coded augmented AFDM (CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM ) scheme, along with a corresponding joint support and symbol detection algorithm. In this scheme, SVs are represented by constant-weight codewords that feature a fixed Hamming weight and a large Hamming distance, resulting in relatively small SV sets. Simulation results compare various SVC/ESVC schemes and diverse coding schemes employed by the CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM, including Hamming, BCH, RS, and polar codes, for QAM symbol protection. The results demonstrate that the proposed scheme provides a distinct reliability advantage over conventional SVC/ESVC schemes, achieving a gain of up to 14 dB. Furthermore, the study indicates that the CWC's weight and minimum Hamming distance must be carefully selected to balance detection reliability, QAM modulation order, and sparse recovery feasibility, thereby maximizing the overall system's performance.

nominations.title: Recursive Semi-Blind Receivers for Wideband Array Processing
nominations.authors: Eleftherios Kofidis
nominations.abstract: Using the commonly employed uniform rectangular array (URA) as an illustrative example, we have recently shown that the block-term tensor decomposition (BTD) model provides a natural representation for the output signal of a multi-dimensional separable sensor array structure in the presence of channel multipath. A palette of effective and efficient semi-blind joint channel estimation/data detection (JCD) algorithms for URA processing, which wed BTD modeling with existing JCD schemes, has thus been developed, and recently extended so as to be applicable in large-scale arrays and/or time-varying environments. However, both the model and the algorithms were based on the assumption of narrowband signals, arriving through paths of effectively the same delay. In this paper, recursive JCD algorithms for wideband sources are developed and evaluated through simulations in a time-varying setting and across different constellation sizes, in comparison with their batch counterparts and the training-only-based solution. They are seen to enjoy the ability to track channel variations and detect the transmitted symbols `on the fly', with the aid of only a short initial training stage.

nominations.title: Dynamic Structural Causal Models for Delay Prediction
nominations.authors: Niloofar Mehrnia, Wilson Ayyanthole Nelson, James Gross
nominations.abstract: Dynamic network key performance indicators (KPIs) such as end-to-end (E2E) delay are shaped by both contemporaneous interactions and temporal persistence. While standard predictors can forecast KPIs under a fixed regime, proactive network management requires reasoning about the effects of explicit actions (interventions) and, in time series, executing a model forward over multiple horizons. We study dynamic structural causal models (DSCMs) for E2E delay in a 5G measurement campaign, where payload and background traffic are intentionally manipulated and thus treated as do-interventions. We learn DSCM scaffolds using four time-series causal discovery methods representing score-based and constraint-based paradigms and common lag-based baselines. Using gradient-boosted decision trees, we evaluate true multi-step DSCM rollout, which recursively simulates the full system state, and a direct target-only ablation that predicts the KPI without recursive simulation. Across two held-out intervention scenarios, including high payload and 10 Mbps background traffic, we find that the inferred target parent/lag sets differ substantially across methods and that rollout behavior is strongly scenario-dependent. In particular, PCMCI+ achieves the best short-horizon rollout accuracy under the payload intervention (RMSE 2.97~ms) but exhibits pronounced horizon-dependent degradation under the background-traffic intervention (root mean squared error (RMSE) ~4.75 ms for long horizon), yielding a large positive rollout tax of up to ~0.78 ms relative to direct prediction; DyNoTEARS and VAR-based DSCMs remain comparatively stable under rollout. These results highlight that evaluating causal scaffolds only via direct prediction can be misleading, and therefore, executability under intervention and long-horizon error propagation are critical for DSCM-based KPI reasoning.

nominations.title: Channel Prediction Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network with EVT-based Adaptive Quantile Loss Function
nominations.authors: Niloofar Mehrnia, Parmida Valiahdi, Sinem Coleri, James Gross
nominations.abstract: Ultra-reliable low latency communication (URLLC) systems are pivotal for applications demanding high reliability and low latency, such as autonomous vehicles. In such contexts, channel prediction becomes essential to maintaining communication quality, as it allows the system to anticipate and mitigate the effects of fast-fading channels, thereby reducing the risk of packet loss and latency spikes. This letter presents a novel framework that integrates neural networks with extreme value theory (EVT) to enhance channel prediction, focusing on predicting extreme channel events that challenge URLLC performance. We propose an EVT-based adaptive quantile loss function that integrates EVT into the loss function of the deep recurrent neural networks (DRNNs) with gated recurrent units (GRUs) to predict extreme channel conditions efficiently. The numerical results indicate that the proposed GRU model, utilizing the EVT-based adaptive quantile loss function, significantly outperforms the traditional GRU. It predicts a tail portion of 7.26%, which closely aligns with the empirical 7.49%, while the traditional GRU model only predicts 2.4%. This demonstrates the superior capability of the proposed model in capturing tail values that are critical for URLLC systems.

nominations.title: Linear Dynamic Range Extension for Rydberg Atomic Receiver via Band-Limited Reconstruction
nominations.authors: Meng Fang, Lebin Chen, Jun-Rong Chen, Ming-Min Zhao, Bin-Bin Wei
nominations.abstract: Rydberg-atom receiver offers a promising approach to radio-frequency (RF) signal reception in wireless communication and sensing systems, combining high sensitivity with the potential for broad frequency coverage. However, the limited linear dynamic range (LDR) of the atomic system causes nonlinear distortion at high input signal levels, thereby restricting the receiver's effective linear input range. To address this issue, we analyze the mechanisms underlying nonlinear distortion in Rydberg atomic receivers and propose a physics-informed band-limited iterative reconstruction (PI-BLIR) method. Specifically, by exploiting the known nonlinear atomic response and signal bandwidth prior, we formulate a constrained maximum-likelihood problem to reconstruct the distorted complex intermediate-frequency (IF) waveform. With the bandwidth constraint absorbed into the frequency-domain parameterization, the constrained maximum-likelihood problem is transformed into an unconstrained optimization problem, which is solved using gradient descent. The proposed method relies solely on digital post-processing and requires no changes to the local-oscillator (LO) field strength, optical parameters, or atomic operating conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that PI-BLIR extends the receiver's LDR by more than 14 dB and enhances the demodulation performance of the atomic receiver.

nominations.title: How Robust are Pinching-Antenna Systems to Practical Deployment Imperfections?
nominations.authors: Amy S. Inwood, Peter J. Smith, Hyundong Shin, Michail Matthaiou
nominations.abstract: This paper investigates the robustness of pinching-antenna systems (PASSs) to three practical deployment imperfections: pinching-antenna (PA) positioning errors, imperfect channel state information (CSI), and line-of-sight (LoS) blockages. We develop analytical frameworks to quantify the performance degradation caused by each imperfection. For PA positioning errors, we employ a Brownian meander model to characterize the distribution and mean of the resulting signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) loss. The results show that positioning errors can diminish the gains from long-term position selection, with the loss becoming more pronounced under stronger shadow fading. For imperfect CSI, we characterize the distribution and moments of the true scattered channel power at the position selected using noisy channel estimates. The resulting selection penalty is governed by the ratio of noise variance to the number of channel measurements, while the upper tail of the selected channel power retains the same behavior as under perfect CSI. Finally, we develop a spatially consistent blockage model and derive the distribution of the optimum long-term SNR for arbitrary blockage configurations, together with a numerically tractable expression for a single blockage. Simulation results validate the analyses and highlight a fundamental property of PASSs: although positioning errors and imperfect CSI can reduce the gains from position selection, good performance can still be achieved provided that an LoS link is available. In particular, even when a large proportion of the waveguide is blocked, PA repositioning can establish LoS links and enable performance close to that of a fully unblocked system for the considered configurations.

nominations.title: Physical Prior Mismatch in Variational Dual-Polarization Quantum SATCOM Channel Estimation
nominations.authors: Anders M. Buvarp, Stefan Werner
nominations.abstract: Dual-polarization quantum satellite communications require accurate estimation of complex polarization channels. We investigate physical latent-prior mismatch in variational estimation of a $2\times 2$ complex channel, using eight Cartesian latent coordinates and a fixed latent-to-channel mapping. Gaussian, matched and sharpened Rician, Laplace, and Cauchy priors are compared under a fixed neural architecture and forward Kullback-Leibler objective. Models are trained for 300,000 updates with $\zeta=1/(2N_{\mathrm{est}})$ and evaluated using three training seeds and 10,000 shared held-out blocks per operating point. The Gaussian and Rician priors coincide at the Rayleigh limit. At higher Rician factors, the matched prior improves estimation accuracy, especially with fewer pilots. At $K=100$ and $N_{\mathrm{est}}=32$, the matched Rician variational estimator reduces mean squared Frobenius error by 2.50% relative to linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE). We also derive a joint Rician Bayesian posterior-mean estimator that incorporates the complete least-squares noise covariance and reduces posterior integration to one-dimensional quadrature. It improves on LMMSE by 3.33% at the same operating point and achieves lower observed error than the scalar Rician and both neural estimators at all 12 operating points. Additional Rician prior sharpening increases error, while Laplace and Cauchy controls remain near the Gaussian baseline.

nominations.title: Joint Optimization of Antenna Partitioning and Distortion-Aware Precoding for Massive MIMO-OFDM with Peak Cancellation and In-Band Distortion Compensation
nominations.authors: Zhuoran Li, Osamu Muta, Haris Ga\v{c}anin
nominations.abstract: In massive MIMO-OFDM systems, peak cancellation (PC) reduces the peak-to-average power ratio but introduces in-band distortion, where compensation signals transmitted from a subset of antennas can suppress this distortion at the users. However, their effectiveness depends on the antenna partition and compensation precoder, while nonlinear power amplifiers (PAs) generate additional distortion. This paper proposes a joint optimization method for antenna partitioning and distortion-aware compensation precoding. To enable this joint optimization, we derive a covariance-based analytical model of PC and PA distortion to predict the per-user, per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plusdistortion- and-noise ratio (SIDNR). The predicted SIDNR is used to select the compensation precoder regularization, the disjoint antenna partition, and the number of compensation antennas. Numerical results demonstrate that joint optimization of the antenna partition and compensation precoder regularization improves BER and SIDNR-based spectral efficiency compared with fixed-partition designs, particularly at high signal-to-noise ratios.

nominations.title: BladeSEI: A Multi-Channel and Multi-Day Dataset for Robust Specific Emitter Identification of Radars
nominations.authors: Ryan White, Robert Jones, Hassan Habib, Matthew A. Ritchie, Victoria Nockles, Adam Hosford
nominations.abstract: This paper introduces "BladeSEI", a multi-channel receiver, multi-day dataset of radar pulses recorded over-the-air from 12 Software Defined Radios (SDRs) for the purpose of Specific Emitter Identification (SEI). The aim of this dataset is to enable investigation into robust SEI techniques that are able to generalise across different receiver channels and recording sessions. The dataset consists of two waveform types per emitter, a 50 microsecond chirped pulse of 40 MHz bandwidth and a 10 microsecond unmodulated pulse. Pulses are captured simultaneously on four synchronised analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) channels of a multi-channel receiver over three recording sessions on two days: a baseline session, an identical repeat on the following day, and a session in which the emitters were thermally conditioned to alter their operating temperature. Initial results using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Inception and ResNet based classifiers, trained and tested on a single ADC channel and recording session, show that the BladeRF emitters can be discriminated at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), with ResNet achieving a macro-F1 above 0.98 at 25 dB for both waveforms, and performance degrading towards random guessing at 0 dB.

nominations.title: An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications
nominations.authors: Rubem Vasconcelos Pacelli, Rodrigo de Lima Florindo, Felix Antreich, Ant\^onio Macilio Pereira de Lucena
nominations.abstract: Audio frequency-shift keying (AFSK) is a widely adopted modulation scheme for CubeSat systems due to its favorable bandwidth efficiency and implementation simplicity. However, coherent detection usually is avoided because synchronization impairments, caused by intense line-of-sight (LOS) dynamics inherent in low Earth orbit (LEO), may significantly degrade the bit error rate (BER). This paper presents a new all-digital coherent AFSK demodulator based on a Kalman filter (KF) for carrier phase and timing delay synchronization and the Viterbi algorithm for bit detection. The Viterbi algorithm is employed for maximum likelihood sequence detection, and the detected bit statistics are fed back to the KF to estimate phase shift, Doppler frequency shift, and Doppler drift induced by the LOS dynamics. Original mathematical analyses are derived to provide a theoretical foundation for the proposed demodulator's operation, specifically addressing its synchronization accuracy in dynamic LEO environments. The proposed demodulator is evaluated considering an additive white Gaussian noise channel with real CubeSat orbits. The performance results obtained through computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed model can withstand such scenarios with a gain of 5 dB in terms of BER compared to the conventional noncoherent AFSK demodulator. The KF performance is assessed using a moving root-mean-square error (MRMSE) statistic and the trace of its state error covariance matrix estimate.

nominations.title: Analytic spread complexity in three-level systems and the spacing-ratio distribution
nominations.authors: Pratik Nandy
nominations.abstract: The spread complexity characterizes the spreading of a quantum state over the Krylov basis and has been proposed to capture the correlations between energy levels. How such correlations manifest in the dynamics has been studied mainly numerically for large matrices. Here we consider three-level systems, the smallest setting with spacing correlations, and derive exact results for the spread complexity, the Krylov variance, and the Krylov entropy. At infinite temperature, the Krylov basis depends on the spectrum only through the ratio of consecutive level spacings, and the spectral variance enters only as an overall time scale. For Gaussian ensembles, these variables are statistically independent, and the averaged spread complexity and variance reduce to one-dimensional integrals over the spacing-ratio distribution encoding the level statistics. We establish universal late-time values of the complexity and variance, and an algebraic relaxation with exponents set by the Dyson index. We also outline the extension to $d$ levels, with the ensemble-averaged spread complexity expressed as a $(d-2)$-dimensional integral over the joint distribution of consecutive spacing ratios.

nominations.title: Quantum violation of Causal Friendliness in the instrumental scenario
nominations.authors: Emanuele Polino, Giulia Lelli, Aaditya Datar, Marwan Haddara, Davide Poderini, Giorgio Milani, Sergei Slussarenko, Howard M. Wiseman, Nora Tischler, Eric G. Cavalcanti, Fabio Sciarrino
nominations.abstract: How far can quantum theory depart from a classical worldview? Bell inequality violations show that no theory can simultaneously uphold absoluteness of observed events, freedom of choice, relativistic causality, and classical causal explanations. While generalized notions of causality, capable of incorporating quantum resources, can account for Bell correlations, the Local Friendliness theorem showed that, in extended Wigner's friend scenarios, the conflict between quantum theory and causal explanations persists even after classical causality is abandoned. This revealed a new form of nonclassicality stronger than what was revealed by Bell's theorem. However, Local Friendliness has been confined to Bell causal structures so far, and it remains unknown whether a related form of nonclassicality persists in more general causal networks. Here we answer this question by considering a Wigner's friend version of the instrumental network, a paradigmatic causal structure in which communication between parties is allowed, and, unlike the Bell scenario, relativistic causality does not impose any restriction. We show, both theoretically and in a proof-of-principle photonic experiment, that quantum correlations are incompatible with Causal Friendliness, which is the conjunction of the absoluteness of observed events and the generalized nonclassical causal constraints imposed by the network. Such constraints extend relativistic causality from Bell scenarios to networks of arbitrary structure. These results establish a form of quantum nonclassicality stronger than previously observed in instrumental-network violations of classical causality, generalizing Local Friendliness beyond Bell-Wigner scenarios and uncovering a new class of correlations with potential applications in future quantum technologies.

nominations.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
nominations.authors: Chao Yin, Vedika Khemani
nominations.abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $\Omega(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

nominations.title: Optically-induced electric Aharonov-Bohm effect
nominations.authors: Gabriel P. Martins, Herman Batelaan, Pablo L. Saldanha
nominations.abstract: Although it was proposed almost 70 years ago, the electric version of the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect, where the interference pattern of quantum charged particles is affected by electric fields that do not interact locally with them, was never experimentally implemented. Here we propose a feasible way to experimentally verify such an important effect, for an electron double-slit interferometer with the slits carved in a nonlinear crystal. The AB phase is generated by a quasi-DC electric field induced in the crystal with the passage of a light pulse (the optical rectification effect) while the electron is superposed in the two slits. We show that this procedure can change the interference pattern of a ensemble of electrons even if they are subjected to negligible electric fields during their propagation, considering feasible parameters.

nominations.title: QuantumInputOutput.jl: A Julia framework for input-output theory with quantum pulses and the SLH formalism
nominations.authors: Christoph Hotter, Orjan Ameye, Klaus M{\o}lmer
nominations.abstract: The interaction of traveling photonic pulses with quantum systems is a fundamental process for many quantum technologies such as quantum communication, control, and measurement protocols. The so-called SLH formalism, named for the triple of operators that parametrize the dynamics, in combination with virtual emission and absorption cavities provides a general toolbox to describe such processes. However, modeling open quantum systems driven by propagating quantum pulses becomes cumbersome once several components, channels, and temporal modes are involved. Here we present QuantumInputOutput.jl, an open-source framework that automates this derivation process: first, symbolic expressions for the Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators are derived using predefined SLH rules and symbolic quantum algebra. Next, the obtained operators are converted to (time-dependent) numerical matrices or are used to obtain higher-order mean-field equations. The numerical expressions are presented in a form immediately suitable for solving the time evolution of the master equation and analyzing the output modes via correlation functions. Besides its usefulness for numerical simulations, the framework also provides a convenient tool to derive symbolic expressions for one-dimensional quantum systems such as multilevel emitters in cavities or waveguides.

nominations.title: Efficient quantum-circuit simulation of classical control of computational order
nominations.authors: Rapha\"el Mothe, Jessica Bavaresco
nominations.abstract: We show that quantum circuits with classical control of computational order admit an efficient simulation by fixed-order quantum circuits: any such transformation acting on $N$ independent quantum channels can be deterministically, exactly, and universally simulated using at most $N^2$ queries. We generalize these constructions to extended, bipartite quantum channels and quantum instruments, and demonstrate that they can be implemented catalytically, without consuming the additional $N^2-N$ queries required for the simulation. In the case of quantum circuits with quantum control of computational order, we prove a similar simulation result, but restricted to unitary input channels (hence non-universal). These results show the limitations of the computational power of these classes of transformations in the studied scenarios.

nominations.title: The radical pair mechanism can generate nuclear-spin entanglement
nominations.authors: Rishabh, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Christoph Simon
nominations.abstract: The radical pair mechanism is a quantum-mechanical process underlying weak magnetic field effects in chemical and biological systems. While nuclear polarization and electronic entanglement in this mechanism have been studied extensively, the possibility of creating entanglement between nuclear spins has, to the best of our knowledge, remained unexplored. Here, we show that nuclear-spin entanglement can develop from initially maximally mixed nuclear spin states and evolve over repeated radical pair cycles. Its generation and persistence depend on the initial electronic state, the available reaction channels, and the interplay between recombination rates, hyperfine interactions, and the magnetic field. We demonstrate this behaviour in both a minimal two-nucleus model and a five-nucleus model inspired by the photosynthetic radical pair P700--$A_1$. Radical pair mechanism generated nuclear-spin entanglement offers a potential new resource for quantum technologies and opens avenues for exploring its role in biological systems.

nominations.title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
nominations.authors: Christina Psaroudaki
nominations.abstract: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter. Phase-cycled Bell-state relaxometry isolates the signed contribution of correlated relaxation to the joint ground-state population. To second order in the probe-environment coupling, the resulting population contrast measures a finite-time integral of the energy-ordered cross-correlator. In the longitudinal regime, XY8 covariance probes the complementary symmetrized cross-correlator within a tunable frequency window. For a gapless quantum spin chain, the signals reveal interaction-dependent algebraic scaling and ballistic propagation. Luttinger-liquid theory links sign changes as the qubit frequency is swept to the propagation time between the probes. It also predicts distinct spatial power laws for the Bell signal before the correlation front and at late times, when the sensing window resolves the qubit frequency. Matrix-product-state calculations for the spin chain test the pre-front scaling at zero and finite magnetization and extract the propagation velocity from Bell oscillations at zero magnetization. The probe coupling geometry determines which spin and momentum sectors contribute to the measured signals.

nominations.title: Finite-time spectral enhancement of transient quantum thermometry
nominations.authors: M. Tahir Naseem, Asghar Ullah, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl\i o\u{g}lu, Mehmet Cengiz Onba\c{s}l\i
nominations.abstract: Transient quantum thermometry extracts temperature information before a probe reaches thermal equilibrium. We study how finite interaction times affect thermometric precision for a harmonic-oscillator probe prepared in a number state and weakly coupled to a thermal bosonic reservoir. A second-order time-convolutionless master equation retains the finite-time reservoir response, allowing modes away from the probe frequency to shape the populations and their temperature dependence. For the baseline parameters, this response raises the quantum Fisher information about fivefold above the Markovian prediction, in agreement with an exact solution of the model. When the probability of leaving the initial state is small, we derive an analytical condition for this enhancement. To assess its operational significance, we examine the temperature information acquired per unit time. Under the exact dynamics, this rate is largest within the reservoir memory time. With negligible preparation and readout overhead, the optimum is about five times the best Markovian rate and 30 times an upper bound on the equilibrium rate. The advantage survives smooth switching, although overhead and longer coupling ramps reduce it.

nominations.title: Recursive Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz
nominations.authors: Lennart Binkowski, Stuart Flannigan
nominations.abstract: The recursive quantum approximate optimisation algorithm~(RQAOA) shrinks an unconstrained combinatorial optimisation problem by eliminating one variable at a time, guided by correlations measured in variational quantum states. We extend this recursion to constrained problems by building on the quantum alternating operator ansatz, which restricts the evolution to feasible solutions through a feasible initial state and feasibility-preserving mixers. However, every elimination alters the feasibility structure, so that such a mixer for the original problem generally fails to be one for the subproblems. Previous extensions to Maximum Independent Set and Minimum Vertex Cover sidestep this with tailored reduction rules that keep every subproblem within the original problem class. We resolve this by identifying, for a given constraint structure, a broader problem class that is closed under all eliminations, and by efficiently constructing feasible initial states and feasibility-preserving mixers for every class member. We do so for monotone constraints, such as for the knapsack problem, for linear equality constraints with polynomially bounded weights, including Hamming weight constraints, and for combinations of equality constraints with a single inequality constraint, such as the cardinality-constrained knapsack problem. Conversely, we show that these restrictions cannot be lifted in general without leaving the realm of efficient constructions. Exact simulations on knapsack and vertex-weighted max-bisection instances demonstrate that our recursive scheme can outperform both its non-recursive counterpart and penalty-based QAOA and RQAOA.

nominations.title: DRAG-Inspired Single Flux Quantum Control of Superconducting Qubits
nominations.authors: V. Vozhakov, M. Bastrakova, A. Liniov, D. Kulandin, N. Klenov, I. Soloviev
nominations.abstract: Scalable control remains a major challenge for superconducting quantum processors due to the wiring, thermal load, and hardware complexity associated with conventional microwave-based architectures. A framework for qubit control based on Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) digital electronics is presented. For transmon qubits, optimized control sequences are constructed from regular pulse trains framed by arbitrary subsequences (ramps), enabling DRAG-inspired leakage suppression in the discrete SFQ regime through genetic-algorithm optimization. For representative $Y_{\pi/2}$ gates, the resulting sequences achieve simulated coherent-control infidelities below $10^{-4}$, including leakage from the computational subspace. The objective of the proposed approach is to demonstrate that coherent errors intrinsic to SFQ control can be reduced to a comparable level for a more scalable cryogenic control architecture. Memory requirements are reduced by storing only the optimized ramps, while a modular controller architecture supporting both regular and arbitrary pulse generation is proposed. The logical complexity of this architecture is estimated from the Josephson-junction counts of its constituent SFQ cells. The proposed approach therefore combines low coherent-control error with reduced memory overhead and provides a basis for scalable cryogenic SFQ control architectures.

nominations.title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
nominations.authors: Yves H. Kwan
nominations.abstract: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<f<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

nominations.title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
nominations.authors: Daisuke Miki, Alfred Li, Yiqiu Ma, Yubao Liu, Yanbei Chen
nominations.abstract: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

nominations.title: Quantum Data Processing Unit for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
nominations.authors: Pranav Srinivas Murali, Russell Marroquin Solares, Warren Zhou, Wanda Hou, Anil Bilgin, Yi-Zhuang You
nominations.abstract: Quantum computers need real-time classical processing to convert measurement data into feedback within device-specific timing constraints. We introduce the quantum data processing unit (QDPU), an architecture between a quantum device and its controller. Its core is a machine-learned quantum data model (QDM), adapted to the measurement response and noise characteristics of the device. We implement an FPGA pipeline for neutral-atom array assembly that performs occupancy detection and rearrangement scheduling in FPGA logic. One calibrated matched-filter lane classifies a $50\times50$ array in 12.5 $\mu$s. An atom-loss model using a software reference planner evaluates a $35\times35$ target with a 60 s trap lifetime and 0.1% loss per moved atom. Removing an assumed 150 ms host round trip raises the predicted assembly success from 8% to 85% and reduces the wall-clock time per successful assembly from 19 s to 0.16 s. A GPU-based outer loop is proposed for refitting model parameters between runs. Its NVQLink transport is measured on the board: over 10 GbE to an NVIDIA DGX Spark, the median FPGA-to-host-to-FPGA round trip is 2.74 $\mu$s for 128-byte messages forwarded by a CPU core. A separate 12-bit learned qLDPC kernel is placed and routed for the same FPGA target, with a derived latency of 0.84 ms per round for a $[[1122,148]]$ lifted-product code under code-capacity noise. A quantised GraphMP ranking kernel for the same code runs on the board with a median host-to-FPGA-to-host latency of 50.5 $\mu$s with one shot in flight, excluding host-side BP+OSD post-processing. Together, these implementations illustrate a shared architecture with workload-specific models and timing requirements.

nominations.title: Fast forward-and-backward creation of non-equilibrium Gibbs state in driven dissipative quantum systems
nominations.authors: Katsuhiro Nakamura, Otabek Normukhamedov, Iwan Setiawan, Jasur Matrasulov
nominations.abstract: We present the fast-forward (FF) approach to adiabatic time evolution of an open dissipative quantum system within the framework of the Gorini-Kosaakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation.
